comments.author: @TheEarthEngineOfficial
comments.text: The reversal is what stays with me — in 1966 Rhodesia was more than twice as rich per person, yet today Botswana is about three times richer, on the same plateau and with far less to start with. The diamonds-under-the-Kalahari detail seems to be the hinge: making them belong to the whole nation rather than a few. I wonder how much of the gap is really about that one decision, and how much is about what came after it — and whether Botswana's recent diamond slump shows the same model now being tested in reverse?

replies.author: @TheEarthEngineOfficial
replies.text: That's a strong correction, and I think you're right — ownership on paper means little if the money leaks out through a few hands. Botswana's side of the story does seem to be the management: the revenue actually reaching schools, clinics and roads. Which part of that machinery do you think mattered most — the institutions that guarded the money, or the political will to let them?
